title: How to Receive USD Payments When You Live Abroad
summary: Money without borders. Send, spend, and save across borders with Blaze, built for nomads, expats, and global businesses.
body_markdown:
You're a freelancer or remote worker living abroad. Your clients are in the US. They pay in USD. And your local bank account was not designed for this situation.


This is one of the most common financial frustrations for expats and nomads in Latin America — and it has a clean solution that most people don't know about.


---


## 🚫 Why Your Local Bank Account Doesn't Work


When you open a bank account in Mexico, Colombia, or Brazil, you get a local account number. That account is set up to receive local currency transfers — SPEI in Mexico, PSE/ACH in Colombia, PIX in Brazil.


It is not set up to receive USD directly.


When a US client tries to send money to your local account:


- Many banks reject the transfer outright
- If it does go through, it comes as an international wire — with fees on both ends
- Your bank converts at their rate, not the mid-market rate


> **US clients can't Zelle, ACH, or Venmo a Mexican bank account. Those payment rails simply don't connect.**


---


## 💳 What Doesn't Work (And Why)


### Local Latin American Bank Account


As described above — not built for USD receipts. International wires are expensive and slow.


### Bank Wires (SWIFT)


This does technically work, but it costs $25–45 per incoming wire on the US side, and your bank may charge another $10–25 on the receiving end. On a $500 payment, that's 7–14% in fees before exchange rate differences.


### PayPal


PayPal does let you receive USD. But:


- Withdrawal to a local bank account costs ~2%+ in fees
- Exchange rate markup adds another 2–4%
- Total cost: **4–6% per payment**


That's $40–60 on every $1,000 you receive.


### Wire Transfers from Clients


Your clients probably prefer ACH — it's free for them or near-free. International wire transfers are an extra step and an extra cost for them. Some clients will pay for it, many won't.


---


## ✅ The Clean Solution: A US Virtual Account


Blaze gives you a **US virtual bank account** — a real routing number and account number, denominated in USD, that your clients can use to pay you just like any other US bank account.


Here's what that means:


- Clients can pay you via **ACH** (free, common)
- Clients can send **domestic wire** ($0–15 instead of $25–45 for international)


The money lands in your Blaze account in USD. From there, you can:


- **Hold it in USD** and convert when the rate is favorable
- **Send it to your local account** in pesos, COP, BRL, etc. at Blaze's 0.5% flat rate
- **Pay others directly** in their local currency without converting first

1. **Download Blaze** and sign up (takes about 5 minutes)
2. **Verify your identity** — standard KYC process
3. **Get your US virtual account details** — routing number and account number

Your clients don't need to do anything unusual. From their side, they're sending money to a US bank account. That's it.
